unit.title: 2D Shapes
unit.blurb: Properties of quadrilaterals, the parts of a circle, and rotational symmetry.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify, describe, classify and sketch quadrilaterals, including trapezia and kites, using their properties.

O2.t: Know the parts of a circle: centre, radius, diameter and circumference.

O3.t: Identify rotational symmetry in familiar shapes and find the order of rotational symmetry.

p: A **quadrilateral** has 4 straight sides. Look at **sides** (equal? parallel?), **angles** (right angles?) and **diagonals**.

A **trapezium** has one pair of parallel sides. A **kite** has two pairs of equal sides next to each other. A **parallelogram** has two pairs of parallel sides; a **rhombus** is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides.
A square has four right angles, so it is a special rectangle (and a special rhombus too).

p: The **centre** is the middle point. The **radius** goes from the centre to the edge. The **diameter** goes all the way across through the centre.
**diameter = 2 × radius**. The distance all the way round is the **circumference**.
The radius is half the diameter. Do not mix them up.

p: A shape has **rotational symmetry** if it looks exactly the same after a turn of less than a full turn.
The **order** of rotational symmetry is how many times it fits onto itself in one full turn. A square has order 4; a rectangle has order 2.
A shape that only fits onto itself after a full turn has order 1 (no rotational symmetry).
